description:

User decisions, 2026-10-11 (with kicad-parts-9693, which uses them to guess a new part's category):
- The category is the only grouping engineers see. In KiCad each category is one group of the part chooser (a database sub-library, shown as <library name> - <category>), and the Catalog's own symbols are grouped by category, as in the CSV catalog today. Footprints and 3D models get no category: footprints are grouped by package, and each 3D model goes with its footprint (kicad-parts-f397).
- Each category keeps a short rule list that people can edit: reference letters (with aliases such as IC for U and S for SW), footprint name patterns (KiCad names such as R_0603* and IPC-7351 names such as RESC*), and keywords.
- Each time someone confirms a part's category, the Catalog keeps the clues that led to it (the supplier category, the footprint family, the reference letter and the manufacturer) as remembered matches for that category, so the guess gets better with use. A DigiKey, Mouser or LCSC category becomes a remembered match only when a person confirms it, never an automatic change of category (criterion 4 of plan pl-ca81).
- The rules and remembered matches start from the existing catalog, its 21 CSV categories and their parts, so the guess works from the first new part.
- Changing a part's category never changes its IPN (glossary: IPN prefix).

Spec, 2026-10-11 (orchestrator's best judgement during the autonomous run; scope for this seed, so kicad-parts-9693 can build on it):

Categories as data
- The CSV import creates one category per CSV file, with a stable ID derived from its code: code (the file name without g- and .csv, such as res), a plain name (res Resistors, cap Capacitors, ind Inductors, dio Diodes, opt LEDs and optoelectronics, trs Transistors, reg Voltage regulators, pwr Power ICs and relays, ics Integrated circuits, ana Analog ICs, mcu Microcontrollers, mpu Processors and modules, osc Crystals and oscillators, con Connectors, swi Switches, cpd Circuit protection, rvr Potentiometers and trimmers, rfm RF modules and shields, mec Mechanical parts, art Board artwork, pcb Bare boards; check each name against the parts in its file and adjust if a name misleads), the IPN prefix new parts get by default (the code in capitals), and its fields: the CSV file's columns in order. A new part in a category gets exactly those fields.
- Categories are revisioned like other Catalog records: each change is a Change with a reason, and history shows it. In this seed only imports change them (a CSV header change); editing rules and names in the app is a follow-up.
- Each part's category is part of its part details (so history, conflicts and CSV reviews work as for any detail; no revision). The import sets it from the CSV file. Changing it in Edit part: a Category choice listing the plain names. The part keeps every field it has; fields the new category has and the part lacks are added blank; nothing is dropped; the IPN never changes. If the CSV later moves the row to another file, that is a CSV change like any other (applied when the part was not edited in the app, otherwise the CSV review notice).
- The local team server (local-team-server) imports every CSV file, not only g-res, so every category exists when trying the app by hand. Keep its start-up time reasonable and say in the guide what it imports.

Category guess (the engine; its UI is in kicad-parts-9693)
- A pure Rust function in crates/catalog: given the clues a downloaded part offers (reference letter, footprint name or names, symbol name, description, keywords, manufacturer, MPN, and an optional supplier category), the categories with their rules, the remembered matches, and the existing parts, it returns every category ranked, each with a score and a reason in plain words (for example: footprint CAPC1608 matches 12 parts in this category). Deterministic: same inputs, same answer; no network.
- Layers, most reliable first: (1) remembered matches people confirmed, and the same MPN already in the Catalog; (2) footprint name patterns (KiCad and IPC-7351 names); (3) the reference letter, with aliases (IC = U, S = SW); (4) similarity to existing parts: description words, keywords, footprint family and manufacturer, with the closest parts voting; (5) a supplier category only through a remembered match.
- Starting rules per category are a small table in code (shipped as the category's initial rules): reference letters (R res, C cap, L ind, D dio, LED/D_LED opt, Q trs, Y osc, J/P con, SW/S swi, F cpd, RV rvr, U nothing), footprint patterns (R_*, RESC* res; C_*, CAPC* cap; L_*, INDC*, INDM* ind; D_*, SOD*, DIOM* dio; LED_*, LEDC* opt; Crystal*, XTAL*, OSC* osc; Fiducial*, TestPoint*, MountingHole* art; ...) and a few keywords each. The existing parts are the starting examples: no stored rows needed for them.
- Remembered matches: a stored record each time a person confirms a category for a clue (supplier category, footprint family, reference letter, manufacturer), with who and when; recorded when someone changes a part's category (this seed) or confirms a new part's category (9693). A supplier category never changes a part's category by itself (criterion 4): it only becomes a remembered match when a person confirms it. Test that.
- Measure it on the real catalog, leave one out: for each of the 178 parts, guess from only the clues a download would give (its symbol's reference letter, footprint name, MPN, manufacturer, description) with that part removed from the examples. Report top-1 and top-3 accuracy in the test output and in a mulch record; aim for top-3 of at least 90 percent; improve the rules if it falls short, and say which categories are hard.

Out of this seed: the Add part screen and showing the guess (9693); editing rules and names in the app, and who may (a follow-up, with kicad-parts-5514); KiCad sub-libraries per category (kicad-parts-f397); supplier lookups by MPN.
closeReason: Merged: categories are revisioned Catalog records created by the CSV import; a part's category is in its part details with a Category choice in Edit part; remembered matches recorded by the server on category changes; the category guess engine (layered clues, leave-one-out top-1 88.2 percent, top-3 98.9 percent with ties counted against it); local-team-server imports every CSV file or a chosen list. Review passed after fixes.

title: Resolve symbol and footprint references through KiCad library tables
description:
Follow-up from the a553 review (finding F1). crates/kicad-integration/src/resolver.rs resolves LIB:NAME in the repo's symbols/ and footprints/ first, then in KiCad's data folder. It ignores sym-lib-table, fp-lib-table and KICAD10_* path variables.

title: Make kicad-cli preview exports single-flight, bounded and self-cleaning
description:
Follow-up from the a553 review (findings F2 and F3), in crates/kicad-integration/src/preview.rs.
- Clicking quickly through parts that share a symbol runs duplicate exports for the same cache key, and N clicks can start up to 2N kicad-cli processes. Stale requests are never cancelled.
- Staging folders left by a crash (staging/<pid>-<n>) are never swept.
- The cache is never evicted across KiCad versions or library edits.
- On Windows the cache shares %LOCALAPPDATA%\org.kicadparts.desktop with WebView2's EBWebView.

Add per-key single-flight, a small concurrency limit, cancellation of superseded requests, a startup sweep of staging folders, and an eviction policy.

title: Persist the collaboration replica checkpoint and detect a dropped last event
description: From the b355 review: the replica keeps its checkpoint in memory only, so a restart reads everything again. description:
Follow-ups from the b355 review:
- Superusers can still write collab_records and collab_changes directly, because null rules don't stop them. An admin edit then leaves a gap in the change log, and every replica fails permanently with 'the change log skips'. Add a hook that blocks direct writes and only allows the protected command route.
- Correlation IDs are global, so another user can tell whether an ID was used (they get correlation_reused). Scope them per user.
- Document that pocketbase superuser upsert takes the per-run superuser password on its command line. Other processes run by the same user can see it while it runs, and the PocketBase CLI offers no stdin option.

title: Keep the zero-loss report working after re-imports
description:
Follow-up from the fef6 reviews. The zero-loss report only holds after a first import:
- Unchanged parts keep the source of the older file, so a later import of a changed file fails with 'Source names another version'.
- After a supplier-only change (nothing_changed), the report shows the old LCSC value as stored.
- The main-manufacturer-part check matches stale incomplete-main-manufacturer-part problems (tooling/catalog-import/src/zero_loss.rs:397-407), so filling in a blank MPN reports a false loss.
- A nothing_changed run records no file hashes, because its audit entry has no sources.
- Inserting, reordering or removing CSV rows breaks the match by row number, and removed IPNs produce no import problem.
Needed before the full-catalog import (kicad-parts-357b).
closeReason: Re-imports stay lossless. Each import run records exactly what it read (files, hashes, header, rows, the commit and the import problems it found), and the report rebuilds the CSV from the latest run, matches rows by IPN and checks symbols against the current library files. All five listed problems are fixed, plus the reviewers' symbol, earlier-problem, row-count and file-hash cases. Two high-effort reviews with three fix rounds. Verified by the orchestrator: fmt, clippy -D warnings (native and wasm), 194 tests, import check, lossless pilot, 26/26 hidden journeys. Follow-ups: kicad-parts-7348, kicad-parts-d838.

title: Make catalog revisions immutable in the store
description: Follow-up from the fef6 reviews. Members cannot write catalog collections, but superusers can still PATCH or DELETE revisions, Changes, audit entries, sources and IPNs, because no hook blocks it. The tests rely on this: tooling/catalog-import/tests/pocketbase_import.rs:500-542 relabel a Change's kind and overwrite a revision's source to simulate edits. Add hooks that refuse updates and deletes on revisions, blobs, Changes, audit entries and parts' IPNs. Replace those test PATCHes with the real edit and restore routes from kicad-parts-2254.
closeReason: Delivered in seed/kicad-parts-2254 and verified. Superusers get 403 when they try to PATCH, DELETE or create Catalog records through the record and batch APIs. Server code cannot update or delete them, except moving a part's current revision to the next one. The collection API refuses deletes, renames and any change to an existing field's definition. Test PATCHes were replaced with the real edit and restore routes.

title: Make CSV imports check the current revision they expect
description: Follow-up from the fef6 reviews. mx-88ce27 says commands carry the current revision they expect, but CSV imports compare each part only with its stored current revision. An import from an older checkout therefore adds revisions that undo newer imported details. Send the expected current revisions with each import, or refuse a new revision when the source commit is older than the current revision's.
closeReason: CSV imports send the current revision they expect for every part and the import run they checked against, and get a 409 if either moved. The importer refuses files from a commit the latest import does not include, and imports that would undo recorded uncommitted changes, unless the override is set; the override is recorded on the audit entry. Git missing, not a repository, and side-branch cases have plain messages. Reviewed and verified with 9496.

title: Decide how CAD item revisions are numbered when content returns to an earlier version
description: Open decision from the fef6 re-review. CAD item revision IDs come from their content (infra/pocketbase/pb_hooks/catalog_csv_imports.pb.js), so a footprint changing A to B to A reuses revision 1. The glossary says every change, including restoring, adds a new revision, and that the current revision is the newest. Option 1, recommended because it is simpler for people: number CAD item revisions like parts, so going back to A adds revision 3 while the bytes stay stored once. Option 2: keep content-based revisions and add a CAD-item exception to docs/contexts/catalog/CONTEXT.md. The user merged fef6 with option 2 behaviour and has not decided yet.
closeReason: User chose option 1 on 2026-10-10: number CAD item revisions like parts, with bytes stored once and the current revision always the newest. Implementation: kicad-parts-54d5. KiCad check: database libraries refer to Library:Name with no revision, so KiCad uses whatever the library file holds, and KiCad Integration must write each CAD item current revision.

title: Prepare the import route and CSV columns for the full catalog
description:
Follow-ups from the fef6 reviews, needed before kicad-parts-357b:
- The route hashes blobs in JavaScript at about 3–5 s per MiB, plus base64 overhead. PocketBase's request-body limit will cap single-request imports of real 3D models (not verified).
- An empty 3D-model file fails the whole import with 400 instead of becoming an import problem.
- Other categories have extra MPN columns (rfm 'MPN2', rvr 'MPN TBC') that would fall into part details instead of becoming manufacturer parts.
- Excluded from BOM is never set; the ART category notes say 'does not appear in BOM'.
closeReason: Import ready for the full catalog. UTF-8 blobs are hashed with PocketBase's own SHA-256: all 13 real 3D models import in under 0.7 s, down from 14.4 s, with an explicit 32 MiB limit checked by both the client and the route. An empty 3D model is an import problem. Extra MPN columns (MPN2, MPN TBC, and any unrouted MPN header) are import problems. Excluded from BOM is set only from KiCad's own symbol and footprint flags; disagreeing footprint choices are an import problem. Column routing covers all 21 CSV files, and every file pilots losslessly. Reviewed with fixes. Verified by the orchestrator: fmt, clippy -D warnings (native and wasm), 208 tests, import check, lossless pilot, 26/26 hidden journeys. Open user questions: is MS128-10F a Würth part, and should ART-0001-0006 be Excluded from BOM? Follow-ups: kicad-parts-ccc0, kicad-parts-e4bd.

Rename them to the glossary terms, for example 'CSV catalog' and 'import problem', so code and conversation use the same words. Keep the oracle's byte and semantic checks unchanged.

title: Let part edits add new CAD item revisions
description:
Split from kicad-parts-2254 criterion 2, which asks for any needed CAD item revisions. Today an edit can bind Symbol and Footprint only to CAD item revisions the Catalog already has, and naming an unknown one gets 400. Allowing an edit to upload a new CAD item or CAD item revision depends on how CAD item revisions are numbered, which is the user decision in kicad-parts-9e05.

Decisions, 2026-10-11 (orchestrator's best judgement during the autonomous run; needed by kicad-parts-9693):

What the user does
- In Edit part, the Symbol and the Footprint each get a Use a file... control (a plain file input, so journeys can set it through WebDriver; no native dialog). Symbol accepts .kicad_sym; Footprint accepts .kicad_mod; anything else is refused with a plain message.
- A .kicad_sym can hold several symbols: if it holds more than one, the form asks which (preselecting the one named like the current reference, else the first). The app shows the preview of the chosen symbol or footprint (kicad-cli, as for team previews) before saving.
- The app fills the reference from the file: the name is the symbol's or footprint's own name; the library is the current reference's library when that is one of the Catalog's g- libraries, otherwise a suggestion: for symbols g-<category of the part's CSV file> (e.g. g-res), for footprints g- plus the KiCad library for its package (R_* to g-Resistor_SMD, C_* to g-Capacitor_SMD, L_* to g-Inductor_SMD, D_* to g-Diode_SMD, LED_* to g-LED_SMD, SOT-*/SC-70/TSOT to g-Package_TO_SOT_SMD, SOIC/SO/SSOP/TSSOP to g-Package_SO, QFN/DFN to g-Package_DFN_QFN, BGA to g-Package_BGA, else ask). The engineer can change the library part before saving.
- Same reference as now and different content: a new revision of that CAD item. A new reference: a new CAD item with revision 1. Content identical to the CAD item's current revision: nothing new (the binding keeps its number), as the import does.
- A footprint whose (model ...) points into the Catalog's 3d-models folder (${GITPLM_PARTS}/3d-models/...) that the Catalog does not have asks for the model file too (.step, .stp, .wrl); the engineer can skip it, and the model then stays unresolved, shown as a missing 3D model. Paths into KiCad's own models stay external, as in the import.
- Save as today: one Change with a reason. The part gets a new revision bound to the exact new CAD item revisions; Excluded from BOM is worked out from the new bytes. History shows the new CAD item revision and the uploaded file name (as its Source). License: unknown, needs review, as for imports.
- Other parts that use the same CAD item keep their exact binding (moving them is kicad-parts-10a7). The success message says how many other parts still use the older revision.

Server (POST /api/catalog/edits)
- The cad section may carry uploads: for each, the role (symbol, footprint, 3d-model), the reference, and the bytes (text or base64, exactly as the import route sends blobs, with the same size limits). The server never trusts the client's reading: it checks a symbol upload is exactly one top-level (symbol "NAME" ...) whose NAME matches the reference, with the KiCad format version it came from; a footprint upload is a whole .kicad_mod whose (footprint "NAME" ...) matches; a 3D model is any non-empty bytes whose key is the 3d-models path the footprint names. title: Make a revision mean a CAD change, and archive instead of restore
description: User decisions, 2026-10-10 (glossary updated in docs/contexts/catalog/CONTEXT.md). Old products must keep the exact parts they were designed with, while new designs use the newest. (1) A part revision is the exact symbol, footprint and 3D model revisions a part uses. Only a change to CAD adds a part revision. CAD content that is the same under a newer CAD item number is not a change. (2) Part details (description, value, datasheet) and manufacturer parts belong to the IPN and are shared by every revision. Changing them is recorded in the history (Change and audit entry, with who, when, why and before/after) but adds no revision. (3) A part that can no longer replace the old one (different package, pinout or value) gets a new IPN, not a revision. (4) Restore goes away. A bad revision is archived instead: hidden from KiCad and the app so nobody new picks it, still found by designs that use it, never deleted. The current revision is the newest revision that is not archived. (5) The IPN never carries the revision. Today every part details change adds a full revision (mx-88ce27) and the desktop has Restore (2254); both change here. Write a plan for the user to approve first: data model, migration of existing revisions, edit and conflict rules for shared details, import rules with the edits-win decision (kicad-parts-75a5), the desktop history, archive and roles (kicad-parts-5514).

title: Give KiCad one library entry per part revision
description:
User decision, 2026-10-10. KiCad stores the name of each placed library entry in the design, and Update Symbols from Library and Update Footprints from Library fetch again by that name. So that an update never switches a design to a newer revision, KiCad gets one entry per part revision, named with the IPN followed by _v and the revision number, for example RES-0000-0470_v2 (check against KiCad naming rules; a colon is never allowed). The same applies to symbol and footprint names for CAD item revisions, for example R_0603_v2. The IPN field and the BOM keep the plain IPN, with the revision in its own field. The current revision of each part goes in the main library; older revisions that are not archived go in an older-revisions library; archived revisions go in a hidden library (KiCad library tables can hide a library from the part chooser while placed parts still find it), so nobody new picks them and Update from Library still works in old designs. Moving a design to a newer revision is always a deliberate choice. Choose between a KiCad database library (.kicad_dbl, see the kicad-integration reference record) and generated library files. Depends on kicad-parts-bd76.

User decisions, 2026-10-11 (research: KiCad Library Convention rules S1.1, F1.1, F9.3 and S2.3, and the KiCad 10 database library docs):
- Footprints are grouped by package and mounting, with KiCad's library names such as Resistor_SMD, Capacitor_SMD, Package_SO, Package_TO_SOT_SMD and Connector_PinHeader_2.54mm, never by part category. One package serves many categories (KiCad's SOT-23 is the default footprint of 341 symbols in 12 symbol libraries), and a copy per category drifts apart. When KiCad's own library has the footprint, parts use KiCad's; how it stays exact when KiCad updates its libraries belongs with kicad-parts-76c3.
- 3D models get no group of their own: each one goes with its footprint, in <footprint library>.3dshapes, named like the footprint (KLC F9.3), so the two can never disagree.
- Symbols made by the team are grouped by part category, and parts are grouped by category in KiCad's part chooser, so the category is the only grouping engineers see (kicad-parts-ae44).
- With a database library, turn on globally_unique_keys (new in KiCad 10) from the first release, so a part can move to another category without breaking the designs that use it. Switching it on later breaks the links in existing designs.
- Settled 2026-10-11: nothing is in production, so designs placed from the old CSV catalog layout need no fallback. kicad-parts-82ea regroups the CSV catalog itself (footprints by package, 3D models with their footprint, team symbols by category), so the import reads it already grouped.

Note from the kicad-parts-3b8b review, 2026-10-12: CAD item names now come from files people upload in the app. The server refuses unsafe names (one colon, plain halves, no traversal or control characters), but names Windows refuses as file names (CON, NUL, COM1, a trailing dot or space) are still accepted; when writing team libraries to disk, refuse or encode them.
closeReason: Built per-team KiCad database libraries: one entry per revision, team-code names such as MA-Parts, relative model links, safe updates while KiCad is open, a desktop section and a CLI. Three review rounds. Follow-ups: 3a04, f6b4, 7e0f, b37d, 092b.

title: Add a part from downloaded CAD files
description:
User decision, 2026-10-11. An Engineer adds a new part from the CAD files they downloaded (SnapEDA, Ultra Librarian, SamacSys / Component Search Engine, or a manufacturer site), without editing a CSV file or committing anything.

1. Add part: drop in the ZIP or the files. The app finds the symbol (.kicad_sym), the footprint (.kicad_mod) and the 3D model (.step, .stp or .wrl), shows the symbol and footprint previews (through kicad-cli, as today), and checks that the footprint links to the 3D model. Vendor layouts differ (a KiCad/ folder means SamacSys, KiCAD/ means Ultra Librarian); files for other CAD tools are ignored.
2. The app fills in what it can from the symbol fields (MPN, manufacturer, value, datasheet, description; downloads often carry only a few of these) and guesses the category (below). The engineer confirms the category, and the app offers the next free IPN for it. An IPN is never reused.
3. Checks before saving, each with a way forward:
   - the MPN is already in the Catalog: open that part, or add the MPN as another manufacturer part of an existing part;
   - the footprint matches one the Catalog or KiCad's own library already has (same pads): use that one, so the library does not fill with near-copies;
   - the symbol pin count differs from the footprint pad count;
   - no license: record Unknown, needs review, never a blank;
   - the footprint group (by package, see kicad-parts-f397) is suggested from the footprint name, and the engineer confirms it. 3D models get no group of their own: each one goes with its footprint.
4. Save with a reason: one Change holding part details 1, revision 1, and revision 1 of each new CAD item. The Source records the downloaded file names and the website. Excluded from BOM is worked out as for every revision.
5. KiCad gets the part through kicad-parts-f397.

Category guess. Research, 2026-10-11: real tools rarely guess well from the description alone (Ki-nTree's fuzzy match defaults to exact matches only; Binner's keyword score often falls back to Other); the ones that work match a few clues and keep each choice a user confirms (inventree-part-import saves it as a new alias; Part-DB matches alternative names). Score each category from these clues, most reliable first:
   1. remembered matches the team confirmed earlier (kicad-parts-ae44), and the same MPN already in the Catalog;
   2. the footprint name: KiCad names (R_0603*, C_0805*) and IPC-7351 names (RESC*, CAPC*, INDC*, LED*) settle most passive parts;
   3. the symbol reference letter: R, C, L, D, Q, J, Y and K are clear; U says nothing; aliases such as IC for U and S for SW;
   4. similarity to existing parts: compare the description, keywords, footprint name and manufacturer with the parts in the Catalog, and let the closest parts vote. This is what tells chip categories apart, such as regulators from MCUs;
   5. later, optional: the DigiKey or LCSC category of the MPN, through a remembered match.
Select the best guess and show why (for example: Chip capacitors, because footprint CAPC1608 matches 12 parts in this category), offer the next two guesses and a search of all categories, and leave the field empty when no clue matches. The engineer always confirms, and confirming teaches the app. No AI service and no network: it works offline and gives the same answer every time. Downloads carry no category and few fields, so for chips expect the right answer in the top three rather than first.

Who: Owners and Engineers add parts; anyone else can send a change request (kicad-parts-5514). Depends on kicad-parts-3b8b (uploading new CAD items) and kicad-parts-ae44 (categories, their rules and remembered matches).

Spec details, 2026-10-12 (orchestrator's best judgement during the autonomous run; builds on kicad-parts-3b8b for CAD files and kicad-parts-ae44 for categories and the guess engine):

Where and who
- An Add part button in the team catalog, shown only to people who can edit. It opens the Add part form in the right-hand column, like Edit part.

Reading the download
- A plain file input (journeys set it through WebDriver; dropping files on the form is a nice extra, not required) that takes a .zip, or loose .kicad_sym, .kicad_mod, .step/.stp/.wrl files.
- ZIPs are read in memory, never extracted to disk: entry names are only labels (no paths are joined), nested ZIPs and files for other CAD tools are ignored, and there are limits (for example 200 entries and 100 MB uncompressed in total; refuse beyond with a plain message). Use a well-known Rust zip crate.
- When the download holds several candidates (two symbols, two footprints), the form lets the engineer pick, as Edit part does for symbols.
- Symbol fields fill the part details, matching property names without regard to case and the common vendor spellings: MPN, Manufacturer_Part_Number, Mfr Part Number; Manufacturer, Manufacturer_Name; Datasheet; Description or ki_description; Value. Only fields the category has are filled; the rest are shown as found in the download so nothing is silently lost.
- Where it came from: detected from the ZIP layout (SamacSys KiCad/, Ultra Librarian KiCAD/, SnapEDA) when possible, otherwise an optional Where from field; it is recorded as the Source with the file names.

Category and IPN
- The category guess (ae44 engine) runs on the clues from the download; the form preselects the best guess with its reason, shows the next two as quick choices and a list of all categories, and leaves it empty when nothing matches. Confirming records the remembered matches (ae44).
- IPN: the app offers the next free IPN for the category's prefix: the next unused middle number with variant 0001 (as ICS-0047-0001), which is how most categories number new designs. The engineer can type another IPN (for example a value-coded resistor variant such as RES-0000-4702); the format and uniqueness are checked as they type. The server refuses an IPN that already exists (someone may have taken it meanwhile), and the app then offers the next free one.

Checks before saving (each with a way forward, none silently blocking)
- MPN already in the Catalog: show those parts with Open, and Add as a manufacturer part of that part instead (which becomes an edit of that part).
- Footprint already known: if the Catalog has a footprint with the same name or identical pads, or KiCad's own library for that package group has one with the same name, offer to use it instead of storing a near-copy (using KiCad's own makes the reference external, as for imported parts that use Device:R).
- Symbol pin count differs from footprint pad count (counting distinct numbered pads): a warning with both numbers; thermal and mounting pads make some differences normal, so it never blocks.
- License: shown as Unknown, needs review, and recorded so.
- Footprint and symbol library: suggested as in 3b8b (footprints by package as g-<KiCad library>, symbols g-<category code>), editable.

Saving
- New route POST /api/catalog/parts (or an extension of the edit route if cleaner): one Change with the reason, the new part with part details 1 (including the category) and revision 1, and revision 1 of each new CAD item, using the same server-side checks as 3b8b uploads (the server never trusts the client's reading, refuses unsafe names, hashes bytes itself). Same correlation-ID replay rules as edits. Needs the right to edit.
- The new part appears in search and opens with its previews and history; others see it through live updates.

Tests
- Server: create, refusals (existing IPN, bad IPN, unsafe names, not allowed, files nothing binds), replay, remembered matches recorded.
- Rust: ZIP reading with hostile entries (../ names, absolute paths, a ZIP bomb over the limit, nested ZIPs), vendor layouts (build small fixture ZIPs at test time from the repository's own CAD files; don't commit vendor downloads), field mapping, pin and pad counting, next free IPN.
- A journey: add a part from a ZIP, see the guessed category with its reason, accept the offered IPN, save, find it in search with previews and history; and the MPN-already-in-the-Catalog path.
- Note from the kicad-parts-ae44 review: a remembered match's weight is shared with the existing parts that have the same clue, and each confirmation also adds the confirmed part as an example, so for a brand-new footprint family a match levels off at about half its full weight (about 75 of 150). Don't expect the full weight in tests.
closeReason: Merged: Add part reads a downloaded ZIP or files in memory (limits, hostile entries, vendor layouts), guesses the category with its reason, offers the next free IPN for the category prefix, checks MPN duplicates, known footprints, pins against pads and the license, and saves one create Change on the team server with remembered matches. Review passed after fixes.

title: Regroup the CSV catalog: footprints by package, 3D models with their footprint, symbols by category
description:
User decision, 2026-10-11: make the move now. Nothing is in production and nobody uses these libraries yet (the user's KiCad 9 and 10 library tables name no g-* library), so designs placed from the old layout need no fallback. This seed is a deliberate, one-time exception to the rule that the CSV catalog and its CAD libraries stay byte-for-byte unchanged (pl-ca81 criterion 6): the app and the tests still never write to them.

Change the CSV catalog (database/, symbols/, footprints/, 3d-models/) so it follows the grouping decided in kicad-parts-f397 and kicad-parts-ae44:
1. Footprints are grouped by package and mounting: g- followed by the name of the KiCad 10 footprint library where that kind of footprint lives (installed at C:/Program Files/KiCad/10.0/share/kicad/footprints). For example g-SOT:SOT-23-5 becomes g-Package_TO_SOT_SMD:SOT-23-5, g-dio:D_SOD-323 becomes g-Diode_SMD:D_SOD-323, g-res:R_0603_1608Metric becomes g-Resistor_SMD:R_0603_1608Metric, and the QFN, DFN, BGA and SO footprints in g-ics, g-cpd, g-pwr, g-reg and g-qfn go to g-Package_DFN_QFN, g-Package_SON, g-Package_BGA, g-Package_SO and so on. Decide each footprint from its pads and description, not only its name. Footprint names do not change; IPC density variants (-L, -M) stay with their base footprint.
2. 3D models go with their footprint: 3d-models/g-<footprint library>.3dshapes/<footprint name>.step (KLC F9.3), referenced as ${GITPLM_PARTS}/3d-models/g-<footprint library>.3dshapes/<footprint name>.step. Renaming .stp to .step changes only the name. One model used by several footprints (for example a HandSoldering variant) stays one file, named after the base footprint. Footprints that use KiCad's own models (${KICAD9_3DMODEL_DIR}/...) keep their path in this seed.
3. Symbols made by the team are grouped by part category: split g-pas and g-dis into the category libraries of the parts that use them (for example g-pas:R_US to g-res, C to g-cap, L to g-ind, R_Potentiometer_Trim_US to g-rvr; g-dis diodes, LEDs and transistors to g-dio, g-opt and g-trs). A symbol used by several categories goes to the one with the most parts. The unused g-no_bom symbols (Fiducial, MountingHole_M3, TestPoint) go to g-art. Symbols that point at KiCad's own libraries (such as Device:R) stay as they are.
4. Update every reference to match: the Symbol and Footprint columns of the CSV files, default Footprint properties and footprint filters inside symbols, model paths inside footprints, database/parts.sqlite (regenerate it from the CSVs so its semantic hash matches them), and the CSV catalog fixture manifest (cargo run -p csv-catalog-fixture -- write .).
5. Keep everything else byte for byte: CSV quoting, column order, CRLF line endings where files have them, and all other values. Change only the library names and model paths, with byte-level edits, never by re-serializing a CSV.

Not in this seed: pointing parts at KiCad's own footprints when the g- copy is identical (that needs KiCad-library CAD read by the app; kicad-parts-76c3 and kicad-parts-e83f), and the legacy Python gui/ folder, which is not supported and stays untouched. Tests, journeys and their screenshot baselines change only where they show a library name; each changed baseline is inspected and critiqued, never accepted just because a test changed.
closeReason: Merged: the CSV catalog is regrouped (footprints by package as g-<KiCad library>, 3D models in g-<footprint library>.3dshapes next to their footprint, team symbols by category), references kept whole on screen. Review passed after fixes.

title: Find why PocketBase tests sometimes fail to sign in
description: PocketBase sometimes answers Failed to authenticate in a test, then the test passes on rerun. Seen in pocketbase_import on 2026-10-11 (82ea gate) and in two pocketbase_bom tests on 2026-10-17 (357b gate), so it is spreading. Likely a timing race: the superuser upsert after PocketBaseServer::start, or a member made just before signing in, isn't visible yet. Next time, keep the test name and its pocketbase-*.log, then add a short sign-in retry after start or wait until the record is readable. A flaky gate wastes runs and hides real failures.
closeReason: Cause: a port race, where another test's PocketBase answered on our port. Start-up now waits for our own log's Server started line. Loops went from 3 failures to 0 in 60 runs.

title: Offer to move other parts to a new CAD item revision
description:
Orchestrator decision, 2026-10-11 (best judgement during the autonomous run). Follows kicad-parts-3b8b, where an edit can add a new revision of a CAD item but only the edited part moves to it.

When an edit adds a new revision of a symbol, footprint or 3D model that other parts also use (for example a corrected g-Resistor_SMD:R_0603_1608Metric used by 29 resistors), the edit form shows: Also use it in the 28 other parts that use this footprint (each gets a new revision), with the list of those parts. It is ticked by default, because fixing a shared footprint is almost always meant for every part that uses it, and designs are never affected: each design keeps the exact part revision it placed (kicad-parts-f397).

- One Change holds every new part revision, with the same reason.
- Only parts whose current revision binds an older revision of that CAD item move; parts already on it, archived revisions, and parts that bind another CAD item are left alone.
- Each moved part gets a new revision as a normal CAD change (Excluded from BOM worked out again); its part details do not change.
- If any of those parts changes while the form is open, the save answers with a conflict listing them, as for one part, and nothing is written.
- History shows the Change once, with the list of parts it moved.
- Needs the right to edit, like any edit.

title: Find why journey 06 sometimes times out waiting for the symbol drawing
description: Seen 3 times during the kicad-parts-ae44 gate (2026-10-12), then clean for 6+ runs, also with journey 06 importing only g-res, so the heavier server start is ruled out. The wait is in the read-only test (06-team-catalog.test.mjs around lines 520-521), after sign-out, sign-in as the viewer, history, revision 1 and the Details tab; waitForDrawnImages re-queries each poll and refuses busy or problem states, so a timeout means the app showed a spinner or a problem card for 60 s. Commit 7f18e06 makes the harness report what the preview section shows when it gives up: Loading... means a stuck kicad-cli export; Sign in to see this symbol or replaced means a lost redraw, and then the fix is to make the preview effect in apps/desktop-ui/src/main.rs (around 574-720) also redraw when the session changes. Next time it fails, read that report and fix accordingly.
closeReason: Fixed in 835f5ec with kicad-parts-9693: the preview effect now also redraws when the signed-in person changes (the harness diagnostic showed a stale Sign in card).

title: Make the MinIO backup test wait until MinIO is ready
description: Seen twice on 2026-10-12 (during the kicad-parts-9693 gate and its review): crates/collaboration/tests/backup_restore.rs a_backup_in_minio_restores_into_a_blank_instance failed with 503 XMinioServerNotInitialized, then passed when run alone. MinIO answers before it has finished starting. Wait for MinIO's readiness endpoint (/minio/health/ready answering 200) in the native-services start-up (tooling/native-services) before the test uses it, with a bounded timeout and a plain error, rather than retrying the backup itself. A flaky gate wastes runs and hides real failures.
closeReason: Cause: MinIO's /ready answers 200 before storage loads. Start-up now waits for /minio/health/cluster and a signed check. Loops went from 47 failures in 55 runs to 0 in 60.

title: Flag a CSV row whose IPN was already given to a different part in the app
description: Found by QA pass 2 and confirmed in review, 2026-10-12. Add part offers the next free IPN from the team server plus the CSV IPNs the app read once per session (csv_ipns is a OnceLock in crates/catalog-browser/src/lib.rs:232), so while both the CSV catalog and the app add parts, the same IPN can be given out twice (an uncommitted or unpulled CSV row, or a git pull during the session). A later import then treats the other part's CSV row as new values for the part added in the app, and accepting the CSV review would overwrite it with a different part. Fix: (1) the import flags a CSV row for an IPN first created in the app (create Change) whose MPNs share nothing with the part's manufacturer parts as an import problem (ipn-given-to-another-part) instead of new values, with a plain message saying to give the CSV row another IPN; (2) refresh the CSV IPNs when the CSV catalog changes on disk or at least when Add part opens; (3) the guide says to give new IPNs in one place during the move from the CSV catalog to the app.
closeReason: Imports flag a CSV row that has an app part's IPN but none of its MPNs, never merging them. Add part re-reads CSV IPNs at save. The notice gives both ways out and the next free IPN.

title: Check our CAD libraries for items made by hand in KiCad, and for bad 3D model links
description:
User decision, 2026-10-12. Making symbols, footprints and 3D models the traditional way stays supported: an engineer draws a symbol in KiCad's Symbol Editor in one of our g- libraries, a footprint in a g- footprint library, links its 3D model, and commits. The app must then notice what was made by hand and warn about what is wrong. Leave the existing CSV catalog files exactly as they are: no clean-up of today's problems in this seed.

The Catalog already records where every CAD item came from (an import, with the CSV file, row and commit, or a file chosen in the app). So made by hand means: in our g- libraries, but not in the Catalog.

A library check, one pure Rust function used by both the CSV import and the desktop app, compares the CSV catalog folder (symbols/g-*.kicad_sym, footprints/g-*.pretty, 3d-models/**) with the Catalog:
- Not in the Catalog yet (warning): a symbol, footprint or 3D model in our libraries that no part uses and the Catalog does not have. Message like: g-ics:IC_TP4333 was added in KiCad; no part uses it yet. When a CSV row names a missing item and a similar name exists in the same library (one name contains the other, or a small edit distance), suggest it: did you mean g-ics:IC_TP4333? (today g-ics.csv names g-ics:TP4333 while the library has IC_TP4333).
- Symbol to footprint (warning): a symbol whose own Footprint property names a footprint that is in neither our libraries nor KiCad's installed libraries.
- Footprint to 3D model, for each model the footprint names:
  - in our library (${GITPLM_PARTS}/3d-models/g-<footprint library>.3dshapes/) with the footprint's name: fine;
  - in our library under another name (a shared model): soft warning;
  - a path into our library whose file is missing: error;
  - KiCad's own models (${KICAD<n>_3DMODEL_DIR}/...): fine, like KiCad's own footprints;
  - a model embedded in the footprint file: fine;
  - anywhere else (an absolute path such as someone's home folder, a relative path, any other variable such as ${GITPLM_3DMODELS}): error, because it only works on one machine.
- Errors count only for footprints that are new or changed since the last import (not in the Catalog, or bytes different from its newest imported revision). The same problems on footprints already in the Catalog and unchanged are listed as clean-up, not errors, so today's catalog (16 missing model files, 17 unresolved, 3 paths into a home folder) still imports.
- An error stops the import before anything is sent, with a plain list of what to fix, the same way the commit-first rule refuses uncommitted changes. Add part and Edit part refuse a chosen footprint with such an error too.

Where people see it:
- The import prints the check: errors first, then warnings, then the not-in-the-Catalog list and the clean-up count.
- The desktop app, for people who can edit, shows a short line near the search box when the check finds something (for example: Library check: 2 new items, 1 to fix) that opens a Library check view grouped as To fix, Not in the Catalog yet, Worth a look, Clean-up, each item with its library, name, file and a plain message. Not in the Catalog yet items get an Add part from it action, built by the follow-up seed; until then the action is absent.

Tests: the check on fixture libraries built at test time (each finding kind, new vs unchanged footprints, the near-name suggestion), the import refusing on an error and running with clean-up only, today's real catalog producing no errors, and a journey for the Library check view.
closeReason: Merged: a library check (one Rust function for the import and the desktop) lists CAD in our g- libraries the Catalog lacks (power symbols skipped; near-name hints such as TP4333 -> IC_TP4333), symbols whose own Footprint names nothing, and 3D model links (our library fine, shared soft warning, missing or outside our library an error for new or changed footprints, quoted or KiCad 5 unquoted); errors stop the import before sending; today's frozen footprints and CSV files keep old problems as clean-up; the team server refuses uploaded footprints with outside links; editors see a Library check line and view. Review passed after fixes.

title: Add a part from symbols and footprints already in our libraries
description:
User decision, 2026-10-12. Follows kicad-parts-da65 (the library check) and reuses kicad-parts-9693 (Add part).

Add part can start from symbols and footprints already in our g- libraries (made by hand in KiCad, or committed by someone else) instead of a downloaded ZIP:
- From the Library check's Not in the Catalog yet list, Add part from it opens Add part with that item chosen; Add part itself also offers From our libraries next to Choose a download, with a search over the symbols and footprints of our g- libraries that the Catalog does not have yet.
- The engineer picks a symbol and a footprint (either can also be one the Catalog already has); the footprint's 3D model is taken from its own link when that points into our library. The same checks as Add part run (category guess, next free IPN, MPN already in the Catalog, pins against pads, license), plus the library check's findings for these items; an error (a model outside our library or a missing model file) stops the save with the same plain message.
- References stay exactly as in the library (no renaming): the part uses g-<library>:<name> as the files are. The server stores them as CAD items like uploads, with the Source naming the repository file and the commit it was read from. A later CSV import that names the same items with the same bytes finds nothing to change (identical content is unchanged, as in kicad-parts-3b8b).
- The CSV catalog files are never written: the part lives in the Catalog; adding a CSV row is optional.

Tests: Add part from library items end to end (server and desktop), the search listing only items not in the Catalog, a model error stopping the save, a later CSV import with identical bytes finding nothing to change, and a journey.
closeReason: Merged: Add part can start from symbols and footprints already in our g- libraries (Library check Add part from it, or From our libraries search); same checks plus library-check findings; commit-first with git object IDs computed from the bytes read; Source records the repository file and commit; later CSV imports update such items like imported CAD. Review passed after fixes.

title: Refuse library Sources in the edit route, and use a vetted SHA-1 crate
description: From the kicad-parts-37a7 review, 2026-10-13. (1) The edit route parses cad.uploads with the shared editUploads (infra/pocketbase/pb_hooks/catalog_lib.js:416), so a modified client can mark an Edit part upload as source:'library', making a later CSV import treat that revision as imported and replace it with the repository's bytes. Low effect (only its own new revision), but only Add part should record where a file is in our libraries: pass a flag to editUploads so publishEdit refuses library details with a plain message; add a refusal test. (2) crates/catalog-browser/src/git.rs has a hand-written SHA-1 (verified correct on 307 sizes against git hash-object); replace it with RustCrypto's sha1 crate (same family as sha2, already locked) to drop about 50 lines, and avoid the extra input copy.

title: Group the part list by category in expandable sections; close the drawing close-up on an outside click
description:
User request, 2026-10-13 (items 4 and 5 of the user's list).

1. Group the left-hand part list by category in expandable sections (an accordion), for the CSV catalog and the team catalog alike: each section header shows the category's plain name and its number of parts, and opens or closes on click or Enter/Space (a real button with aria-expanded, keyboard friendly).
   - With an empty search, every section starts closed and remembers what the person opened and closed (for the session).
   - While searching, sections with matches open by themselves and show their match count, and sections without matches close (or are hidden, whichever reads better; say which you chose). Clearing the search goes back to what the person had open.
   - Selecting a part (from search, history, a notice, Add part) opens its section and scrolls it into view. Parts only the team catalog has, and new parts, appear in their category's section.
   - Keep the list fast with all 178 parts and with a few thousand (no per-keystroke heavy work).
2. The close-up view of a symbol or footprint drawing (the large modal) closes when the person clicks outside it (on the backdrop), as well as with Escape and its close button; focus returns to what opened it.

Tests: unit tests for grouping and the open/closed rules; a journey covering searching (sections open and close by themselves), clearing, selecting a part in a closed section, keyboard use, axe, and the close-up closing on a backdrop click. Screenshots for the new list look (re-baseline the screenshots whose left column changes, with a critique each).
closeReason: Merged: the part list is grouped by category in expandable sections (counts-only empty search, sections load when opened, 25 per section with Show all while searching, best-matching section first, keyboard focus kept, selected part always revealed); the drawing close-up closes on an outside click. Review passed after fixes.

title: Browse symbol and footprint libraries (ours, KiCad's, installed) with previews and filters
description:
User request, 2026-10-13 (item 3, and the browser that items 1 and 2 need). Orchestrator's design calls follow; build it ourselves, like KiCad's choosers.

A Libraries browser, opened from a Libraries button in the main header at any time (and reused by kicad-parts-bc6f for choosing CAD):
- Left: the libraries, in three groups: Ours (the CSV catalog's g- symbol and footprint libraries), KiCad (KiCad's installed libraries, found as the library check already does), and Installed (other libraries the person has added to KiCad, read from their KiCad library tables: %APPDATA%/kicad/<version>/sym-lib-table and fp-lib-table, with ${KICAD<n>_*} and other path variables expanded from kicad_common.json and the environment; nested tables in KiCad 10 followed). These files are only ever read, never written. Symbols and footprints in separate tabs.
- Middle: the items of the chosen library (or of all libraries, searched), with a search over name, description and keywords, and filters:
  - symbols: pin count (exact or range), reference letter, hide power symbols, has a default footprint;
  - footprints: pad count, SMD / through-hole / both, and, when opened for a symbol, KiCad's own two filters: Match the symbol's footprint filters (ki_fp_filters) and Match the symbol's pin count.
  - Each row shows the name and a short description; items the Catalog already has are marked (In the Catalog), as are items with library-check findings.
- Right: the selected item's drawing (kicad-cli, through the existing preview cache; only the selected item is drawn) and its details: library, name, description, keywords, pin or pad count, footprint filters, the 3D model link for footprints, and which Catalog parts use it.
- Speed: KiCad's own libraries hold tens of thousands of items. Read each library's names and the details the filters need once, in the background, into an index cached in the app's data folder and refreshed when a library file's size or modification time changes; never parse everything on each keystroke. Support KiCad 10's .kicad_symdir symbol libraries as well as .kicad_sym files. Read with the library check's safety (no links followed outside the library, limits on file size and nesting).
- Opened from the header, it only browses: an item not in the Catalog offers Add part from it (kicad-parts-37a7 for ours; the choose seed for KiCad's and installed ones), an item in the Catalog offers Show the parts that use it.
- Keyboard and accessibility: arrow keys move through items, Enter chooses, Escape closes; the browser is a dialog that closes on an outside click like the drawing close-up; axe passes.
- This overlaps kicad-parts-e83f (resolve references through KiCad library tables): reuse one library-table reader for both, and note in e83f what this seed covers.

Tests: the library-table reader on fixture tables (variables, nested tables, missing files, a nickname differing from its file name); the index (build, refresh on change, .kicad_symdir); filters (pin count, pad count, SMD/THT, ki_fp_filters matching with KiCad's wildcard rules, pin count match); tests never read the developer's own KiCad settings (fixture tables only; KiCad's installed share folder may be used read-only); a journey opening the browser from the header, filtering, previewing and closing, with axe.
closeReason: Merged. The Libraries browser lists ours, KiCad's and installed libraries, with previews, filters, a cached index and an exact Parts using filter. Review passed after fixes.

title: Choose symbols and footprints from the Libraries browser in Edit part and Add part
description:
User request, 2026-10-13 (items 1 and 2). Builds on kicad-parts-d152 (the Libraries browser), kicad-parts-9693 (Add part), kicad-parts-37a7 (Add part from our libraries) and kicad-parts-3b8b (files in Edit part). Orchestrator's design calls:

1. No typing CAD names. In Edit part and Add part, Symbol and Footprint show the chosen reference as read-only text with its drawing, plus Choose... (opens the Libraries browser for that role, with the current item selected and previewed so the person sees what replaces what) and, as today, Use a file... for a downloaded file. For footprints opened from a part with a symbol, the browser starts with KiCad's two filters on (the symbol's footprint filters and pin count). For a file that goes into our libraries (a download or an installed library's item), the library is a choice of our g- libraries for that role (the suggested one preselected), not free text; names come from the file. Multi-choice footprints keep a list with Add another / Remove.
2. Add part starts with two choices: Upload a ZIP (as today) or From a library, which opens the browser over ours, KiCad's and installed libraries. Generic parts from KiCad or other libraries have no IPN yet and are not in our g- libraries; Add part gives them a category, an IPN and part details as usual.
3. What choosing an item does, by where it lives:
   - In the Catalog already: used as the Catalog has it (bound to its current revision).
   - In our g- libraries but not in the Catalog: added from our libraries as in kicad-parts-37a7 (commit first; the Source names the file and commit).

   - Another installed library (a personal or third-party one, which teammates may not have): copied into the Catalog as a new CAD item in one of our g- libraries (chosen as above, the footprint's 3D model with it when it is a file we can read), like a download, with the Source naming the library and file. Its 3D model link follows the library check's rules (an outside link is rewritten to our library's place when the model is copied, or the save stops with a plain message when the model cannot be read).
4. The Add part from our libraries search of kicad-parts-37a7 is replaced by the browser; the Library check's Add part from it opens Add part with that item chosen, as now.

Tests: Edit part with Choose... for each of the four origins (server and desktop), read-only fields (no free-text CAD names), the library choice for copied items, Add part From a library for a KiCad generic (external reference, new IPN) and for an installed library's item (copied, Source recorded, 3D model handled), journeys for both flows with axe.

title: Test the browser's link rule with junctions and team values
description:
From the d152 review. Symlinks need Developer Mode, so the link rule has no test that runs here. Junctions need no special rights.

Test three cases with junctions. An installed library whose own path is a link is followed. A junction inside an installed folder is skipped and counted. A junction in our libraries is refused.

Also test the Parts using filter with team catalog values. Read each library table once per read, even when two tables include it.

title: Run kicad-cli with its own KiCad settings folder
description:
kicad-cli reads and rewrites the user's KiCad settings in %APPDATA%\kicad. If it reads kicad_common.json while another KiCad process is saving it, it writes defaults over the whole file. That empties the path variables and resets KiCad's answers. Our app and tests start several kicad-cli runs at once, and this happened on 2026-10-15.

Set KICAD_CONFIG_HOME and KICAD_CACHE_HOME for every kicad-cli run, in run_kicad_cli in crates/kicad-integration/src/process.rs, to a folder the app owns. Exports made this way are the same; I checked by hand. Add a test with a fake kicad-cli that shows the variables are set and are not under %APPDATA%. kicad-cli never gets the user's settings, even for path variables: pass those with --define-var instead.
closeReason: kicad-cli now uses its own settings folder.

title: Footprint close-up with layers, zoom and pan
description:
In the drawing close-up and the Libraries browser, the mouse wheel zooms at the pointer. A drag with the left or middle button pans, and a button fits the drawing again. The keyboard can zoom and pan too. Symbols keep kicad-cli's drawing, zoomed as vector graphics.

For footprints, draw the close-up ourselves from the .kicad_mod, because kicad-cli's SVG has no layers and is cropped. Draw each layer as its own group: copper, paste, mask, silkscreen, fab and courtyard, front and back. A layer list turns each on or off and picks the active layer. Paste and mask follow KiCad's margin and ratio rules, pad first, then footprint. Thumbnails stay as kicad-cli draws them.
closeReason: Footprint close-up draws layers, zooms and pans.

title: Measure between points in the footprint close-up
description:
Add a Measure tool to the footprint close-up. Click two points, and the readout shows the distance, X and Y, in mm or mils. Points snap only to the active layer: pad centres, corners and edge midpoints, and the ends and centres of lines, arcs and circles.

When the two points are on two pads, the readout also shows the gap between the pads on that layer. So switching between copper and paste shows how their gaps differ. Escape clears the measurement. While the tool is on, the left button measures and the middle button still pans.
closeReason: Merged at 7919a26. Two reviews found nothing that must change. The gate passed: 540 tests, 94 journeys and 21 pilots.

title: Show a footprint's 3D model in the app
description:
Wherever the app draws a footprint, a 3D view shows it with its 3D model. Dragging turns it, the wheel zooms, and the middle or right button pans. Say which model file it uses, and why when there is none or the file is missing.

Build a one-footprint board with an outline around the courtyard. Point its model links at the real files: the Catalog's stored model, our library, KiCad's own, or an installed library through the user's path variables. Run kicad-cli pcb export glb with pads, silkscreen and mask, and cache the result like previews. Show it with three.js, copied into the app and never loaded from the network.
closeReason: Merged at a6bb664 after three review rounds. Gate: 568 tests, 104 journeys and 21 pilots passed.

title: Journey 18 fails: the chosen part is out of view
description:
Journey spec 18 (apps/desktop/journeys/specs/18-team-choose-from-libraries.test.mjs) fails on every run since about 2026-10-15. It says CAP-0004-0001 was not shown selected in Capacitors, with inView false. It fails the same way before kicad-parts-3f59, which changed no screen code.

The part is selected in an open section but scrolled out of view. A guess: the list scrolls to the selected part only once (want_scroll in ResultList, apps/desktop-ui/src/part_list.rs). After the add or the Libraries dialog, the list may reload and move the part. Find the cause and fix it. Then the part stays in view.

title: Better advice when kicad-cli's settings folder fails
description:
When kicad-cli's own settings folder cannot be used, the KiCad panel says to check that you can write to it. That is wrong advice when the folder overlaps a KiCad folder. Say both: make sure you can write to it and that it is not inside a KiCad folder (apps/desktop-ui/src/main.rs, near line 520).

Also, when the folder fails only at export time, the preview error says kicad-cli said it was not started. kicad-cli never ran, so drop the kicad-cli said part (run_export in crates/kicad-integration/src/preview.rs).

title: Keep part list focus when a teammate saves
description:
Every team change rebuilds every section of the part list. The outer For in ResultList (apps/desktop-ui/src/part_list.rs) keys each section by query, category and team version. So a focused part row loses keyboard focus whenever anyone saves.

Since kicad-parts-c69c, open sections keep their parts across team changes. So the version can probably leave that key. Check that sections still reload after a team change, and that focus and the selected part stay put.
closeReason: Part list sections and rows are keyed by identity, so a teammate's save keeps focus, selection, open sections and scroll. When focus must move, a note says why. Screenshot numbers are unique and checked.

title: Small Measure tool improvements from the second review
description:
Nice-to-haves from the second review of e95e, merged at 7919a26.
- In mils, a gap under 0.00127 mm reads 0.0 mils instead of touching. Set the touching limit from the unit shown.
- In a small window, N moves the view to a point that is already visible. Pan only when the point is outside the drawing.
- Journey 19's paste-margin step waits less than journey 17 for the Libraries browser. Use journey 17's wait.

title: Tidy the 3D view code after the c9c1 reviews
description:
Small leftovers from the c9c1 reviews, merged at a6bb664.
- Split the long footprint_3d function into smaller steps.
- Share checked_model in model3d.rs with read_model in pick.rs.
- Links like /./x.step or /C:/x.step get the network message. Say the file is missing instead.

title: Keep the 3D view steady: turn around the centre, never fly away
description:
The user asked for this on 2026-10-16. The wheel still zooms at the pointer, but turning always goes around the model's centre, even after zooming or panning.

The view must never end up far away, lost or broken:
- Limit zoom, so the model can't get too small to see or put the camera inside it.
- Keep panning near the model, so the model can't be moved out of view.
- Never let the camera's numbers become invalid, even after many fast wheel turns or drags.
- Reset view always brings back the starting view.

Test long, fast drags and wheel bursts in the journeys, and check the model stays in view.

title: Write ADR files for our hard-to-reverse decisions
description: The user wants decision records in docs/adr/ so the domain-modeling skill finds them. Write one ADR for each decision that is hard to reverse, surprising and a real trade-off, checked against today's code. Each ADR names its mulch records. Replace mulch record mx-bf5787, which said not to create docs/adr/. Fix mx-fe6936, which points at an ADR file that never existed.

title: Show category fields in the older and archived revision groups
description: In the generated KiCad database library (f397), the older and archived revision groups carry only the fields every category shares. Placing a revision from those groups loses fields such as Tolerance. Update from Library keeps the fields a placed part already has, so old designs are not affected. Choose between one older and one archived group per category, which adds groups to KiCad's chooser, and all fields in both shared groups, which leaves empty fields on placed parts. This is the user's choice; give a recommendation.

title: Support symbols that extend another symbol in the KiCad libraries
description: The generated KiCad libraries (f397) leave out a symbol that extends another symbol, and report it. The CSV catalog has none today, but downloads and uploads may. Write each such symbol with the exact revision of the symbol it extends, so a revision never changes when its parent changes (see kicad-parts-d838). Rows that use a left-out symbol must say why.

title: Name the installed ODBC driver in the CSV catalog's database library
description: database/#gplm.kicad_dbl uses DRIVER={SQLite3}, but the driver installed on Windows is named SQLite3 ODBC Driver, so KiCad likely can't load this library. The user doesn't use it today; they use their own MA and SL libraries. Only change it with the user's go-ahead, because agents never modify database/.

title: Keep every team's KiCad libraries up to date at once
description: The user works for several clients at once, and each client is its own team with its own server and team code (f397). The desktop signs in to one team at a time, so only that team's KiCad libraries update. Let the desktop keep every team the person belongs to up to date at once. Decide how several sign-ins work without saving passwords (mx-8ffc3d). Agreed with the user on 2026-10-17.
closeReason: Folded into kicad-parts-f10d, which keeps every team signed in and up to date.

title: Stop a team server from claiming another team's KiCad library folder
description: Each team's KiCad library folder records only its team settings ID (f397), which every member of that team knows. A server the person signs in to could report another team's ID and change that team's rows, for example the footprint of an existing revision. Update from Library in that team's boards would then pull the wrong CAD. Also record the server address in the folder, and ask the person before writing when it differs. Found in the f397 review on 2026-10-17.
closeReason: Merged. A team folder takes updates only from its recorded server. Review passed after fixes.

title: Make new revisions and details name the Change saved with them
description: The write guards in infra/pocketbase/pb_hooks/catalog_write_guards.pb.js check where a part's pointer moves, but a new revision or new details may name any existing Change, even an old one. A future hook could then move a part without a new Change, and desktops that follow Changes would never hear of it, while a sign-in read would. Make the guards require the newest Change, saved in the same transaction, as the archive-entry guard already does. Found in the a3ba review, 2026-10-17.
closeReason: Every new Catalog record must name its own transaction's Change, and saving it moves its part. New parts start empty. Read errors fail closed, and every guard refusal answers 500 and is logged.

title: Let each category choose which field becomes KiCad's Value
description: VALUE_FIELDS in crates/kicad-libraries/src/plan.rs picks KiCad's Value by old category codes (rvr, opt, osc), so a category made later can't choose. Store the Value field on the Catalog Category, next to its fields, and let an editor choose it. When a part has no such value, show something a schematic reader understands: the two art rows now show their IPN, where TestPoint or the description would read better. Found in the 357b review, 2026-10-17.

title: Bring footprint alternatives into the team KiCad libraries
description: Four parts (CPD-0015-0001, ICS-0022-0001, ICS-0025-0001, ICS-0039-0002) list several footprint choices, but only the first is stored, and the others stay bare g- names. With only the team libraries in KiCad, the part places fine, but footprint assignment can't offer the other choices. When a later choice exists in the first choice's .pretty, import it as a CAD item and write the filter with the team's name, such as MA-Package_DFN_QFN:WQFN20_RUK_TEX_v1. Found in the 357b review, 2026-10-17.

title: Show the LCSC part number on KiCad parts
description: Decided by the user on 2026-10-18: KiCad parts show the LCSC part number, because JLCPCB assembly users rely on it in their BOM. The CSV catalog's own library showed it on 67 parts. Show the current LCSC number as a field from supplier data; it never makes a revision, and Update from Library refreshes it. Reword the 357b supplier-data rule's reason, which says supplier data never reaches KiCad.

title: Import the CSV catalog into a running team server
description: Only the throwaway servers of pilot, full-pilot and local-team-server import the CSV catalog today. A team needs one plain command or desktop action that imports into its own server, runs the full proof's checks, and reports in the same words. Reuse import_in_order and the full-pilot checks, then update docs/operations/MOVE_THE_CSV_CATALOG.md so the guide ends with a real move. Found in the 357b review, 2026-10-17.

title: Mark the fields a new category adds in Edit part
description: When a person changes a part's category in Edit part, the new category's fields are added to Part details, but nothing marks which ones are new. In screenshot 60-team-category-choice, Material appears among the resistor's own fields, so a person has to compare by eye. Mark the added fields plainly, for example with a short 'new' note, and say which fields the old category had that the new one doesn't. Found in the ae44 visual review, 2026-10-17.

title: Keep journey screenshots the same whatever the time of day
description: Journey 22's screenshots 90 and 92 failed at some times of day: the time was blanked, but the full stop after it moved with the width of the digits. Found in the 2091 gate on 2026-10-17. Fixed on branch seed/kicad-parts-2091: the harness shows every time as zeros before a screenshot, and journey 22 checks two different times give the same pixels. See mulch mx-1710c5.

title: Find why journeys sometimes fail at launch with a connection reset
description: A journey sometimes fails at launch with 'connection forcibly closed' (os error 10054), before any step runs, then passes on rerun. Seen on 2026-10-17 in journeys 05 (357b gate), 12 (f397 gate) and 14 (2091 gate); mulch mx-625975 records it. It looks like a start-up race between tauri-driver, msedgedriver and the app. Find the cause, fix it once in the journey harness, and prove it with repeated runs under load.

title: Stop journey 13's 960 px check failing now and then
description: Journey 13's 'fits a 960 px window' test fails about 6 times in 23 full runs: axe leaves #footprint-heading unchecked for colour contrast. Mulch mx-3b542d records it. Find why axe can't judge that heading's contrast at times, for example a background not settled after the resize. Fix the cause in the app or the journey, never by turning the check off.
