title: Make turning and zooming feel right when zoomed far in
description: When the 3D view is zoomed far in, a small drag flings the zoomed spot away: at zoom 50 a 20 px drag moves a corner 473 px. Zoom at the pointer is exact only for points level with the model's centre; on top of a 20 mm part it drifts about 6 px per notch. Have the user try a slower turn when zoomed in, for example dividing the turn per pixel by the square root of the zoom. Shift the projection with camera.setViewOffset so zoom at the pointer is exact at every depth. Found in the 4588 review, 2026-10-18.

title: Work with many clients' libraries and catalogs at once
description:
User decisions, 2026-10-18. The user (team MA) designs for many clients. Each client gets its own team server, hosted by the user for now. Many clients have only an ad hoc KiCad library in a git repo.

The app must read and write those libraries in their own layouts. It must copy parts between teams and start a catalog from an existing library. It must keep the person signed in to every team at once, with one search over all catalogs.

title: Read any client's KiCad library repo through a library source profile
description:
User decision, 2026-10-18. Clients keep KiCad libraries in git repos, each laid out differently. Add a repo, as a local clone or an address, and scan it at a pinned commit. Link each team to its library repo in team settings (moved here from f10d).

The scan finds symbol and footprint libraries by file type. Nicknames come from the repo's own lib tables, or else file names. Model path variables come from footprint model links. It also finds any .kicad_dbl file.

The person confirms a one-screen summary and fixes only what the scan got wrong. Save a small profile: repo, commit, libraries, variables, and a short prefix so names never clash.

Make our own layout (symbols/, footprints/, 3d-models/, ${GITPLM_PARTS}) the default profile, read by the library check, import, Add part and Libraries browser. Fold in kicad-parts-e83f.

title: Reach any git host with the person's own git and SSH setup
description:
User decision, 2026-10-18. Client repos may be on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or any git server. The person's SSH key already has access. Use the system git program, as crates/catalog-browser/src/git.rs does, so the app never stores or sees keys.

When a repo is added, confirm it is a git repo and read its remote address. Check read access with git ls-remote and write access with git push --dry-run. Say the result in one line, or which step failed and what to check.

Keep the app's own clone in its data folder. Never write in the person's checkout (mx-70700f). Reading works offline from that clone. Fetching and pushing wait until online, and the app says so.

title: Write parts into a client's library in that library's own layout
description:
User decision, 2026-10-18. Copying parts into a client library with no catalog writes the symbol, footprint and 3D model where that library keeps them.

Suggest rules for where new files go from what most of the repo already does. For example, models may sit next to footprints or next to symbols, under the repo's path variable. The person confirms the rules once per repo.

Write in the app's own clone, commit on a new branch and push. Then open the host's new pull request page in the browser. GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket are known; for other hosts, show the branch name. No API token is needed. A setting for each repo can push to the main branch instead.

title: Stay signed in to several team servers at once
description:
User request, 2026-10-18. The person works for several clients in one day, and must not sign out and in to switch. Sign in once per team server, and keep every session and its live updates running side by side.

Today the token lives only in memory (crates/catalog-browser/src/team.rs). Keep renewable sign-ins in the operating system's credential store, never in a file. This changes an earlier choice, so write an ADR.

The app runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, so use one cross-platform crate. It uses Credential Manager, Keychain or the Secret Service. If Linux has no Secret Service, keep sign-ins in memory only and say why.

Keep every signed-in team's KiCad library folder up to date (ADR 0015). Link each team to its library repo in team settings. A server that can't be reached shows its cached parts marked offline.
closeReason: Merged. Every team stays signed in through the system password store. Review passed after fixes.

title: Search and manage the parts of all teams in one list
description:
User request, 2026-10-18. One search covers every signed-in team's catalog. Each row shows its team code, such as MA or AC, as text plus a team colour, never colour alone.

A team filter at the top offers All teams (the default) or one team. Results can also be grouped by team.

Editing a part always saves to that part's own team, with the person's role there (kicad-parts-5514). Every team request names its team (server address), not the shown team (f10d review). Add part asks which team, starting from the filter or the last team used. Parts move between teams only by copying.
closeReason: Merged. One list and search over every team. Review passed after fixes.

title: Copy parts from one team to another, with origin and license
description:
User request, 2026-10-18. Copy one or more parts from one team, such as MA, into another team's catalog. If the client has no catalog yet, write them into its library (kicad-parts-02fb).

The copy gets the target team's own IPN, and the guess engine suggests its category. Record where it came from: team code, IPN and revision. It is a copy, not a link, so later changes never flow across.

Show each CAD item's license before copying, because downloaded vendor CAD may not be shareable. With both teams signed in (kicad-parts-f10d), the copy goes straight across.

title: Warn when a client's board uses another team's libraries
description:
User request, 2026-10-18. A board must use only its own client's libraries. Otherwise the client cannot open it, and MA's parts leak into their design.

Read the saved project files (ADR 0005). List symbols and footprints from libraries outside the project's team and its library sources. Offer a way forward for each: copy the part to the client (kicad-parts-1a46) or swap it.

Run it on demand and before hand-off. Decide while planning how a project is tied to a team, for example by the client repo it sits in.

title: Start a team's catalog from its KiCad library and past designs
description:
User request, 2026-10-18. This is for a client with only an ad hoc library. Read the library (kicad-parts-e9a3) and the client's saved schematics.

Group the symbol, footprint and value combinations their designs placed into proposed parts. Guess categories with the existing engine (ADR 0010). Offer IPNs in the team's numbering, and let the engineer confirm in batches. Library items no design uses can wait.

Each new CAD item records its source repo and commit. Old boards keep working, because the ad hoc library stays. New designs use the team's code-named libraries.

title: Explain how to move a team server to a client's own machine
description:
User decision, 2026-10-18. For now the user hosts every client's PocketBase on their own endpoint. Each client gets one instance (ADR 0002), with its own pb_data folder and address.

Write steps in docs/operations for handing one over. Stop the server and copy pb_data, as the tested restore does. Run it with Docker on the client's server, then point members' apps at the new address. Include a Docker compose file pinned like infra/versions.lock.

title: Keep each team's last-known parts on disk for offline starts
description:
Follow-up from the f10d review, 2026-10-18. Today an unreachable team server shows its last-known parts only within one run. If the server is down when the app starts, that team shows no parts.

Keep each team's last-known parts on disk, so a start-up with a server down still shows them, marked offline. This adds little exposure, because each team's KiCad library folder already holds its parts. Catch up from the server when it is back. ADR 0018 records the gap.

title: Fix the Windows link error in native desktop-ui builds
description:
Found in the 092b review, 2026-10-18. cargo build -p kicad-parts-desktop-ui fails on Windows with LNK4319: a PDB limit was hit while adding public symbols, after many very-long-symbol warnings.

The shipped UI is wasm built by trunk, so only native workspace builds break. Try debug = "line-tables-only" for that package in the dev profile, or leave it out of default-members. Check that cargo build --workspace works on Windows afterwards.

title: Fix symbol mismatch with KiCad 10.0.7 for entries using Device:R
description:
Found 2026-10-23 after KiCad here updated from 10.0.4 to 10.0.7. kicad_loads_every_generated_library_and_resolves_every_entry fails with lib_symbol_mismatch for RES-0000-0470_v2 and RES-0000-0000_v2 (KiCad's Device:R, R_Small).

kicad_finds_every_entry_of_the_whole_catalog also fails now, on main too (mx-553f4e). Find both causes; work across KiCad versions.
closeReason: Merged. KiCad 10.0.7 bug 25870, partly worked around.

title: Small follow-ups from the one-list review
description:
From the 8a71 review, 2026-10-23.

- Tighten the 10 x 3,000 part search test; 1.5 s per search can't catch a slowdown.
- Cache the Libraries browser's copy of listed parts, not a copy per items request.
- Name apart two servers that show the same team code.

title: Remove the one-thread KiCad test setting once KiCad fixes issue 25870
description:
From the bd98 review, 2026-10-24. KiCad 10.0.7 can give database library entries an empty symbol when their source library loads late (KiCad issue 25870).

The real-KiCad tests set MaximumThreads=1 to avoid it. Watch the issue; when a KiCad release fixes it, remove the setting and the docs note.

title: Find why the import state test sometimes counts 6 requests
description:
Seen 2026-10-24 in a full workspace run. the_import_state_is_read_from_current_records_only in pocketbase_import_state.rs made 6 server requests where it expects 7.

It passed 5 of 5 runs alone, so it looks flaky under load.
